item.title: Re: Multiverse Search Engine
item.content:encoded:
Long expositional tale short he says there was a group of ten, and one got a bit too aggressive. He ended up taking out seven members of the group before he himself fell, and after seeing the deaths of 80% of his friends, one offed himself, leaving one. This one, the D-Class, believes the aggressive one survived and is using the computer to find out.

I have really big concerns about this idea: bringing elder gods into this feels like a really weird mishmash of scales; where you have this like relatively small scale anomaly in the form of a search engine on a single computer coupled with all these grand, universe scale things like gods and a pattern screamer1 and…I'm left feeling like a lot of this narrative feels complex over interesting?

Like my big concern is really 'how are you going to draw in the idea of there being elder gods who had a fight and one of them was cast out so hard that their non-existence is dangerous' here without it feeling almost like a complete non sequitur of a story?

Footnotes
1. which is quite different from nothing btw; like the nonexistence zone you mention in Russia is probably SCP-3930 and it's not just 'a thing that doesn't exist' but 'a thing that actively hates existing'

item.title: Re: Multiverse Search Engine
item.content:encoded:
I may have forgotten to add the Big Story Post (TM).

so here it is; I hope it clarifies things.

+ show block
– hide block

Throughout the logs, a D-Class will be making additional searches, outside the requested ones. The Foundation, wanting to get as much interdimensional info as possible, let's this continue for now.

Eventually, the D-Class only makes his own searches, and he is interviewed to find out why he's not doing what he should be doing.

Long expositional tale short he says there was a group of ten, and one got a bit too aggressive. He ended up taking out seven members of the group before he himself fell, and after seeing the deaths of 80% of his friends, one offed himself, leaving one. This one, the D-Class, believes the aggressive one survived and is using the computer to find out.

All ten of them were elder gods. (No part in the article mentions gods, so a potential name for the article is 'A Tale of Ten Gods'. I have seen other SCPs do this, and there is only one group of ten in the article)

The interviewer does something very uncharacteristic, indicating elder god mind-magic, and the D-Class is permitted to keep searching for the aggressive god.

The D-Class searches for one more thing, but the search term isn't recorded, as the D-Class, satisfied with the lack of results from the final search, looks up one more random thing, causing a massive electric shockwave that kills all personnel present save one, including the god, corrupts the camera footage and causes immense structural damaged to the room.

The Foundation is obviously concerned at a lack of results as mentioned by the survivor, but they don't know what was searched.

Another important note is there are several scps that don't exist, the most memorable is one in Russia, a several km² zone of nonexistance. If the resultless thing is as bad as that, it could have devastating effects. Its also important to note who searched it, if the thing did still exist it could be catastrophic.

item.title: Re: Multiverse Search Engine
item.content:encoded:
Then one test shows no results. Given that keyboard spam still gave results, what is the one thing that doesn't exist in any dimension?

My concern here is like…any interesting thing here has to exist? I'm like, really unsure how 'there is one thing that doesn't exist anywhere' can be interesting because like…surely it has to exist enough for us to know what the implications of it not existing are?

Iunno, my concern is that you've built this big narrative around the foundation trying to find this one test out again with them devoting a lot of resources to it but I don't really have an idea of what the stakes of this are: like, if the Foundation finds the thing, what happens? Why is the answer so important?

On a higher level, AWCY? feel like a strange fit here? They do anart, and it feels like that's pretty far removed from 'writing a strange search engine'? But then, AWCY? have done computer based art before; it's more, the search engine doesn't really feel like an art piece over it being computer based, y'know?

item.title: Re: Multiverse Search Engine
item.content:encoded:
I understand planning tales already is ambitious, and I will try to fit all the story into this one article.

Also, I feel a little clarification is in order:

The electric waves was an example of what might happen if you use it. There are infinite multiverses and therefore infinite methods of communication, and while an infinite amount would be readable to us, and infinite amount would not, and an infinite amount would kill us.

The reason it's a gamble is because the Foundation doesn't know what will happen if you click a link, it could:

  • be normal english
  • be written in a hybrid of french and russian
  • fire a giant laser
  • emit a toxic cloud
  • give you AIDS
  • download a virus

And that's where the test logs would shine: a list of random events that happen when something is searched.

Obviously if you go to "free-money-no-virus.lep.ha" (.lep.ha being an example of otherdimensional websites) and it summons a single gerbil, if you go back to that same website it will summon another gerbil. The effects are based on the equivalent of the .com, so eventually the Foundation could learn what each website will do.

item.title: Re: Multiverse Search Engine
item.content:encoded:
[Placeholder, expect reply in less than 2 days.]

I'm going to give some advice here. Don't plan any tales yet. Write the complete story out in this one SCP article that you're pitching to me, which is your first. Right now, this pitch doesn't deserve multiple derivative tales because it can be a neat anecdote.

In your new idea, you've introduced a lot of stuff that I'm going to try to break down.

This is all told from the Foundation's view, and they know nothing.

So how are the readers supposed to be interested in this story if they are kept in the dark too? If you don't answer any questions and the events are introduced in a seemingly-random manner, like the DClass appearing out of no where, how are readers supposed to connect the dots and deduce that a god is investigating a bureaucratic mishap? By leaving all these answers to be written in a tale later, that's lazy, and you should just focus on how you want to explain this story through this article first, so that readers will be interested enough to even read your next few works.

Because of this it keeps the logs unique every time, as it's a gamble whether or not its going to kill someone.

Please do specify what electric waves are, I don't think electricity can travel through the air unless particles are ionised, and for that to happen, it requires the energy of a lightning strike. That will ultimately transform it into another anomaly altogether, into "The computer that calls Thor's mighty thunder every time someone performs a search on it". I kid, of course, but please do clarify.

Also, you said that a website for another dimension produces these lethal waves every time, so why would it be a gamble for the Foundation? It is literally confirmed they will die, and death without reason isn't really a tense thing anymore. So if these DClass keep dying, what is Foundation supposed to learn about the multiverse?

item.title: Re: Multiverse Search Engine
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the reply.

The AWCY was just a simple origin story, explaining (vaguely) that it was made for an AWCY exhibition, that can be done away with easily with no problems.

There is a goal in mind for the test logs. I didn't have the space for it in the first post, and I got sidetracked by IRL stuff so I didn't make another post, but it goes like this:

Long ago, elder gods, cosmic entities, etc. One god gets too ambitious, and is erased from reality, showing the power of these beings. A few eons later, the last remaining god, who was suspicious that the erased god was never actually erased but managed to escape, finds the Computer in the Foundation. Using some elder-god mind magic, he gains access to the computer as a d-class, specifically the second one. After a few searches, the god finds the one that confirms that the god was indeed erased, and kills himself using the computer. (Explanation later)

+ show block
– hide block

This is all told from the Foundation's view, and they know nothing. They see some D-class turn up out of nowhere just as the first dies, and somehow survives the computer, and searches his own things, and get worried. They don't know what was searched to give no results, so they want to find that search to work out if this absence of a thing is a problem or not.

With luck, I will make a tale on the perspective of the erased god and the god in the Foundation, showing what actually happened (mostly) and that the god was indeed erased. But nature abhors a vacuum, so a new god of the same power as the old one is made to fill that hole. He has no memory and no idea what or who he is.

From here I could go anywhere: tales following this god trying to find who he is, SCP articles of anomalies caused by the unknowable power in this entity, but I can't make the God himself an SCP without tweaking it a lot.

Now the reason the computer is deadly: Data transmission. We communicate through sight and hearing and touch, but what if another dimension has a sense called 'Snorf', where they pick up electric signals to communicate? A website for them would just blast out a wave of electricity, which would be very dangerous to be in. Because of this it keeps the logs unique every time, as it's a gamble whether or not its going to kill someone. The Foundation views D-Class as disposable anyway, so they'll throw a few at this computer until they can answer questions like "How to physics for Fleebians" or something, as the knowledge of the multiverse is worth a few casualties.

So from Elder Gods to Snorf-blasts and Fleebians, I hope that answered your questions. If you have any more, please let me know.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.content:encoded:
[Placeholder]

I don't really see why the anomaly should be in AWCY's hands in the first place? There seems to be no connection apart from, "Oh, we found it there", so I think you can do away with that origin story. Other than that, I feel like the article will get really repetitive if it is just test logs without a solid goal in mind. You tried to introduce tension by introducing a search query that gives nothing, but if it gives nothing, then it simply doesn't exist in the multiverse? Why does Foundation have to care about that? Why would Foundation pump so many resources when they can just keep typing the same query in to give the same result that it simply doesn't exist? What's so frightening about it that would make Foundation so panicked?

Wikidot PM me when you answered the questions in your reply.

item.title: Multiverse Search Engine
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Unsure

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A Foundation raid on an AWCY exhibition results in a strangely built 'computer' coming into containment. It is similar to Google but shows results from any dimension in the multiverse.

Central Narrative: The meat of the article is in the test logs, as anything searched produces an endless number of results, providing the Foundation with knowledge of other dimensions. Then one test shows no results. Given that keyboard spam still gave results, what is the one thing that doesn't exist in any dimension?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation has to try and replicate the result to determine if it poses any threat, becoming more frantic as time goes on, with the Foundation pumping more and more resources into it to solve the mystery.

Additional Notes: I have partly-fleshed out plans for a minor tale series following the mysterious result-less thing, but I won't work on that until this idea does well as an article, if it doesn't then I'll shelve it for a while.
